root_idea.summary: Erasure or wiping away of a thing's visible trace, mark, or form.
root_idea.development: The evidence extends this core from physical effacement to loss of light or sight, concealment, alteration of form, and related figurative uses.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form طَمَسَ rather than the inflected QAC lemma طُمِسَتْ.

senses.definition: To efface, obliterate, or remove a trace, mark, writing, or other visible form; also to become effaced and lose one's visible form.
senses.usage_conditions: Used transitively when a visible trace or form is removed, and intransitively or passively when the thing itself becomes obliterated. Destruction may be expressed as the result of removing the thing's trace or form.

senses.definition: To deprive of sight or light; to blind or cause illumination to disappear.
senses.usage_conditions: Used especially of eyes or sight; the same loss-of-light conception can apply to a celestial body whose light is extinguished or no longer visible.

senses.definition: To transform or alter a thing or person's form, condition, or outward appearance.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic constructions concerning possessions and faces, the action is interpreted as changing or metamorphosing them, with destruction of possessions also reported as an interpretive result.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The heart's becoming bad, corrupt, or morally unsound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed expression describing a heart's deterioration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become distant or remote, or to go far away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive use describing a person's becoming distant or departing to a distance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To look far away, or to look at something from afar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the construction طَمَسَ بِعَيْنِهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cover writing by folding the written material over it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use applied to a written document.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cover or conceal stars, as clouds or mist do, so that they are not seen or their light is obscured.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or extended construction describing atmospheric concealment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Conjecture or computation based on conjecture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also treated as an infinitive associated with the verb's conjectural use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Corruption, or the rendering of something bad or corrupt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical use equivalent to فساد, distinct from physical effacement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Effaced or becoming effaced; said of a relic, remain, mark, trace, ruin, or dwelling whose visible remains are disappearing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of winds that repeatedly efface things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having lost sight or light; an eye or person that is blind, or a star whose light has gone or which is hidden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Of a blind person, it may describe one whose eyelid edge or slit is not apparent; of stars, it can describe disappearance or concealment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Distant or remote; indistinct from afar, or far-extending and pathless.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a mountain not plainly discernible at a distance and to a desert characterized by great extent and lack of paths.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dead or corrupt in heart, or retaining nothing in the mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of a person's inner state or deficient memory.
